Which columns are missing together

Source: R/profile_extra.R
misspat.Rd

Counts the distinct PATTERNS of missingness across rows – which combination of columns is missing in each row – rather than the per-column rates profcols() reports. Use it before deciding how to handle gaps (drop rows, impute, model separately), because the right choice depends on whether columns are missing together.

Usage

misspat(data, maxpat = 20L)

Arguments

data

A data frame whose missingness patterns are counted.

maxpat

Maximum patterns to return, most frequent first, one positive whole number (default 20).

Value

A data frame of class bricklayer_missingness, one row per pattern: pattern (character, . for present and X for missing, in column order), nrows (integer), pctrows (numeric, percent of all rows), n_missing (integer, columns missing in that pattern) and columns (character, their names comma-separated, "" for the complete pattern). Carries the column order as the "columns" attribute.

Details

The distinction decides what to do about the gaps. Two columns each 30% missing at random need different handling from two columns 30% missing in THE SAME rows – the second is one structural gap (a join that failed, a form section nobody filled in) and often means those rows should be dropped or modelled separately, while the first does not. A per-column rate cannot tell the two apart; this can.

Each row is coded as a string with one character per column, X where is.na() is true and . otherwise, and the codes are tabulated. Patterns are sorted by descending frequency and the first maxpat kept, so pctrows may not sum to 100 when patterns are cut. A frame with no rows gives an empty table. The work is one pass over the rows; very wide frames give long codes.

Errors: data not a data frame, without columns, or with missing or duplicated names; maxpat not one positive whole number.

See also

profcols() for per-column rates.

Examples

# Two columns missing in the SAME rows: one structural gap.
structural <- data.frame(
  id = 1:10,
  a = c(rep(NA, 3), 4:10),
  b = c(rep(NA, 3), 4:10)
)
misspat(structural)
#> ╭── Missingness patterns ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Columns   in pattern order: id, a, b                                      │
#> │   Patterns  2                                                               │
#> │   Rows      10                                                              │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   pattern  n_rows  pctrows  n_missing  columns                              │
#> │   -------  ------  -------  ---------  -------                              │
#> │   ...           7  70.0             0                                       │
#> │   .XX           3  30.0             2  a, b                                 │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Each pattern marks the columns missing together; a few large patterns     │
#> │   point to a cause worth naming before rows are dropped.                    │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# The same per-column rates, but missing independently.
scattered <- data.frame(
  id = 1:10,
  a = c(rep(NA, 3), 4:10),
  b = c(1:7, rep(NA, 3))
)
misspat(scattered)
#> ╭── Missingness patterns ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Columns   in pattern order: id, a, b                                      │
#> │   Patterns  3                                                               │
#> │   Rows      10                                                              │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   pattern  n_rows  pctrows  n_missing  columns                              │
#> │   -------  ------  -------  ---------  -------                              │
#> │   ...           4  40.0             0                                       │
#> │   ..X           3  30.0             1  b                                    │
#> │   .X.           3  30.0             1  a                                    │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Each pattern marks the columns missing together; a few large patterns     │
#> │   point to a cause worth naming before rows are dropped.                    │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# A complete frame has exactly one pattern.
misspat(data.frame(x = 1:3, y = 4:6))
#> ╭── Missingness patterns ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Columns   in pattern order: x, y                                          │
#> │   Patterns  1                                                               │
#> │   Rows      3                                                               │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   pattern  n_rows  pctrows  n_missing  columns                              │
#> │   -------  ------  -------  ---------  -------                              │
#> │   ..            3  100.0            0                                       │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Each pattern marks the columns missing together; a few large patterns     │
#> │   point to a cause worth naming before rows are dropped.                    │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# keep only the most common pattern
misspat(scattered, maxpat = 1)
#> ╭── Missingness patterns ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Columns   in pattern order: id, a, b                                      │
#> │   Patterns  1                                                               │
#> │   Rows      4                                                               │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   pattern  n_rows  pctrows  n_missing  columns                              │
#> │   -------  ------  -------  ---------  -------                              │
#> │   ...           4  40.0             0                                       │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Each pattern marks the columns missing together; a few large patterns     │
#> │   point to a cause worth naming before rows are dropped.                    │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# a frame without columns has no patterns
try(misspat(data.frame()))
#> Error : misspat: `data` has no columns
